3910604554.claim: During low-volatility consolidation regimes, the rate of change of normalized volume exhibits negative skewness.
3910604554.verification_plan: Identify low-volatility consolidation periods using a rolling standard deviation of CLOSE returns (e.g., 20-period). Within these periods, compute the 1-period rate of change of volume normalized by its 50-period rolling mean. Test the skewness of this ROC series over a 20-period window. Use a one-sample t-test against a null hypothesis of zero skewness. Report the mean skewness and its statistical significance (p-value).

1682248780.claim: During low-volatility consolidation regimes, the occurrence of a new 20-period low in the rate of change of normalized volume is followed by a significant positive shift in the 5-period shifted rolling maximum of volume within the next 5 periods.
1682248780.verification_plan: Within identified low-volatility periods, flag days where the ROC of normalized volume hits a new 20-period low. For each event, calculate the mean of the 5-period shifted rolling max of volume in the 5 days following the event. Compare this to the mean of the same metric in the 10 days preceding the event. Use a paired t-test to determine if the post-event mean is significantly greater. Report the mean difference and effect size (Cohen's d).

397445701.claim: The time lag between a new low in the rate of change of normalized volume and the subsequent peak in the shifted rolling maximum of volume is less than 10 periods for a majority of occurrences in low-volatility regimes.
397445701.verification_plan: For each event (new ROC low), find the subsequent local maximum in the 5-period shifted rolling max of volume within a 20-period forward window. Calculate the lag in periods. Compute the median and 75th percentile of these lags across all events in low-volatility regimes. Test if the median lag is significantly less than 10 using a one-sample Wilcoxon signed-rank test.

3467057704.claim: The magnitude of the volume spike following a new low in the rate of change of normalized volume, measured by the peak shifted rolling maximum, is positively correlated with the depth of the preceding ROC low during low-volatility regimes.
3467057704.verification_plan: For each event, quantify the 'depth' as the z-score of the ROC value relative to its preceding 20-period distribution. Quantify the subsequent 'volume peak' as the maximum value of the shifted rolling max in the following 10 periods, normalized by the pre-event median. Calculate the Pearson correlation coefficient between these two series. Test its significance against a null of zero correlation using a permutation test. Report the correlation coefficient and p-value.
